# Independent audit: all-point central pairing and the Gamma-level obstruction

Audit of `candidate 42db79d64fa93f5f`.
Result: PASS, with no mathematical correction requested.

The centered-strip comparison follows directly from the actual inclusion
`(A-A)/2` in the centered strip of the same width. Brunn--Minkowski
gives the correct volume direction, including a zero-volume strip and
dimension one. It uses central symmetry of the body, not merely of one
chosen marginal at a preferred point.

For a symmetric marginal, the two shifted tails equal one minus a
translated width-`2s` strip mass when `s>=0`, and one plus the
corresponding strip mass when `s<0`. These identities give the complete
fixed-normal infimum stated in Section 2, with equality attained at
zero shift in the first case and a sufficiently large finite shift in
the second. Since ordinary depth is at most half the volume, taking
the infimum over all normals proves `p_KK(y)=2f_K(y)` for EVERY
deterministic point, including points outside the body.

The symmetric-noise extension is valid for arbitrary independent
symmetric noise without moment or support assumptions. Conditioning
reduces each cap to the already proved average of opposite shifts;
all relevant functions are bounded probabilities. Conditioning also
makes every hyperplane boundary null. No density or weak-convergence
assumption on the noise is hidden in this argument.

For the square pyramid, the change of variables
`(x1,x2,z)=(Z U,Z V0,Z)` gives independent uniform `U,V0` and density
`3z^2` for `Z`. Every positive vertical-coefficient normal reduces to
the displayed clipped function of a symmetric sum of two uniforms.
I checked the uniform-mixture density, its total mass one, both endpoint
degeneracies, and both formulas for the centered-uniform average.

At `c=77/100`, the small-radius branch decreases to a value exceeding
`27/64` by `66973/968256`. On the other branch the exact numerator is

    (5/16)v^3+(63/200)v^2-(123/400)v+146533/1000000.

Its quadratic part has positive leading coefficient and strictly negative
discriminant `-9007533/100000000`, so it is positive for all real `v`;
the cubic term is nonnegative on the needed domain. This is an all-normal
bound, not a test at axial or finitely many normals.

For negative vertical coefficients, reciprocal convexity bounds the
opposite conditional pair below by `2c^3` until one opposite conditional
cap is full. Thereafter the pair is at least one, still greater than
`2c^3`. Purely horizontal normals capture half the mass. These three
cases establish the claimed ordinary depth floor without asserting
that its exact value is `c^3 V`.

The paired axial cap has one zero-volume supporting face and the other
threshold `27/50`, giving exactly `105317V/125000`. Its deficit from
`2 Gamma_3 V` is `607V/500000`. Making the top cap proper raises the
sum by at most `3epsilon V`, while the lower cap shrinks; thus the
stated strictly proper perturbation and residual gap are valid.

Validation: `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_central_pairing_and_grunbaum_level_obstruction.py`
passes the exact scalar and rational certificates. The result is a
pointwise paired-tail obstruction; no mixed-integer source or OC
counterexample is inferred from it.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
